intent: Concept sprite design for review; not installed
generationPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production-oriented transparent 2D weapon VFX sprite atlas for a cute mobile penguin shooter seen from an angled top-down camera. This is EFFECT ART, not gun illustrations, UI buttons, icons, a diagram, or a gameplay screenshot.
Create one beautifully polished coherent atlas containing exactly 21 isolated effect sprites, in a precise 3-column by 7-row equal-cell grid, portrait layout. All seven rows and three columns must be equally sized. Each sprite centered in its cell, consistent visual scale, entirely inside its cell, at least 18% empty alpha margin on every side. No grid lines, no labels, no words, no background. Genuine transparent RGBA background; never paint a checkerboard.
The 3 columns are: compact muzzle flash; a single projectile/beam flying RIGHT with its trail extending LEFT; compact impact flash. This is a still peak-phase frame atlas, not animated frames. Do not draw extra projectile clusters, debris, weapons, penguins, people, skulls, coins, snowflakes or scenery.
Art direction: high quality cartoon action VFX, hand-shaped precise silhouettes and elegant saturated colour gradients, clean cel-shaded luminous forms, a SMALL bright creamy/white inner core (under 15% of the effect area), a rich coloured middle edge, a restrained soft halo and a subtle darker hue boundary so each sprite is clear against pale blue-white snow. Sharp intentional silhouettes, little visual noise, few strong spark shapes. Cohesive with a rounded, dark-navy outlined mobile cartoon game, but avoid heavy black outlines on lights. Each remains readable at 32 to 64 pixels. Moderate impact and colour, no huge blinding white blobs, no concentric wheel/cog designs, no repeated dots that turn the trail into a string of beads, no giant star decoration.
Exact row contents, top to bottom:
Row 1 STANDARD BULLET, warm amber/gold: a tiny asymmetrical four-ray directional muzzle snap; one thin tapered golden streak with a rounded cream tip; a small tight four-point amber impact cross, clearly smaller than an explosion.
Row 2 SHOTGUN, burnt orange/copper: a short wide three-lobe muzzle fan; ONE round copper-gold pellet with a very short tapered trail, not a group of pellets; a compact chunky orange impact flash with three strong short rays.
Row 3 PIERCING, violet/magenta: a sharp narrow violet muzzle flash; a very slender pointed violet energy lance with two clean side streaks, longer and thinner than the standard bullet; a crisp asymmetric violet piercing slash/cross.
Row 4 LASER, emerald/teal with lime accents: a tiny restrained glowing aperture flash; a thin straight emerald beam with a narrow lime-white center, continuous and smooth, NOT a ring or bead chain; a focused teal electric flare with four short pointed rays.
Row 5 EXPLOSIVE, scarlet and hot orange: a short red-orange ignition blossom; ONE glowing ember bolt with a dense orange body, short tail and white tip; a readable compact radial red-orange blast bloom with six irregular rounded lobes, a small bright center, and an outward-moving arc hint, NO debris.
Row 6 MISSILE, deep orange with ruby edges: an elongated orange exhaust ignition flash; ONE sleek fiery comet traveling right, with a defined ruby/orange head and a tapering left exhaust tail, no literal rocket body; a larger rounded orange-ruby blast with a strong scalloped silhouette and two curved wave accents, no rubble.
Row 7 BLAST SNIPER, hot pink and radiant gold: a concentrated gold muzzle star with pink outer tips; a razor-thin hot-pink/gold needle bolt, elegant elongated shape with a tiny bright head; a tight golden core impact with three outward pink-gold arcing rays, powerful but clean.
All 21 are distinct. Keep each row's palette consistent across its three sprites. Different weapons are distinguished by silhouette, length and shape as well as hue. Leave truly empty space between cells. The final image is a clean reusable transparent sprite sheet.
refinementPrompt:

Preserve the exact seven-row order, the three-column muzzle/projectile/impact meanings, each row's colour palette and all 21 effects. Retain genuine transparent alpha; no text, no labels, no backgrounds. Keep the painterly luminous cartoon style.
Make these specific improvements: separate the three effects of EVERY row with generous truly transparent gutters so no halo touches its neighbouring cell. In particular the orange muzzle and comet on row six must be fully separate. Make each sprite a little smaller inside its own equal cell; keep all of its tail. The row-six middle projectile MUST have ONLY ONE clearly defined bright forward head at the right tip and a smoothly tapered left exhaust. Remove the extra rear white head so it cannot read as two projectiles. The row-two middle projectile is a SINGLE compact round amber pellet with a tiny tail, noticeably shorter than a standard bullet. Reduce fine glitter/noisy little specks around all silhouettes, keeping edges clean and one restrained soft halo. Reduce the area of solid white cores, keeping rich saturated middle colours that are visible on pale snow. Make the green laser in row four a smooth thin continuous beam with no bead chain or ring. Keep the red and orange explosion shapes rounded and compact, never covering large areas with white. No new objects, no additional rows or sprites, no debris, no rubble, no guns.
